judged_text: The blacklist and duplicate-attendee comparisons are case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but `guest` is not lowercased before `.includes(guest)`, and `guest === attendee.email` compares raw strings. Adding 'Spam@X.com' when BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains 'spam@x.com' bypasses the blacklist and the guest receives booking emails; adding 'User@X.com' when attendee 'user@x.com' already exists creates a duplicate attendee row and a second calendar attendee, defeating the uniqueness the client-side schema enforces.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but the filter uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so `Spam@X.com` can bypass a blacklist entry `spam@x.com`. Likewise, duplicate detection uses `guest === attendee.email` (raw strings), so `User@X.com` vs existing `user@x.com` will not be detected and can create a duplicate attendee row via `createMany`. The diff shows no normalization to enforce case-insensitive uniqueness/blacklist checks.
